title: Wendell and the Escarpment
premise: Kestrel Nakamura, a disgraced mountain guide living off the grid beneath the Escarpment, is hired quietly by the missing survey team's daughter to find them before the monsoon seals the high passes. Following a river upstream through country he was once banned from entering, he uncovers evidence that the team stumbled onto a falsified land survey—one that would strip an indigenous valley community of its inheritance—and that someone powerful wants the discovery buried along with the witnesses. Hunted by a private security contractor and haunted by the rescue failure that got him blacklisted, Kestrel must choose between staying invisible and becoming the witness the valley needs. In the climax he leads the last survivor and the evidence down through the flood-swollen gorge, sacrificing his escape route, and the story ends with him surrendering to authorities at the trailhead, choosing testimony over freedom as the monsoon breaks.
about_author: Gideon Lockridge is the pen name of a former backcountry ranger who spent a decade leading expeditions across three continents before turning to fiction. His novels are known for their unflinching wilderness realism and morally tangled heroes who find that the hardest terrain is human.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Living under a false name in a river town beneath the Escarpment, Kestrel takes low-stakes work and avoids eye contact. A woman, Mara Voss, finds him anyway, carrying her missing father's compass. The beat is wary isolation cracked open by an offer he should refuse—and can't.

chapters.title: Cold Contract
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He interrogates Mara's story, finds the official search was called off too fast, and agrees to scout the lower river for money only. He retrieves abandoned survey gear bearing fresh bullet holes. The beat is reluctant commitment shadowed by the memory of the expedition that ended his career.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, intercut with Mara's. Upstream, he finds the surveyors' cache: notebooks describing a 'corrected' boundary line and a page torn from the official map. Meanwhile Mara, searching her father's office, realizes his firm falsified the original survey years ago. The beat is dawning dread on both fronts.

chapters.title: The Valley That Remembers
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He reaches the Ashen valley community whose land the falsified survey would seize; elder Suri Oyate recognizes his old guide's insignia and, testing him, shows him the true markers. He learns the missing team included a whistleblower. The beat is shame meeting an unexpected inheritance of trust.

chapters.title: Boots on the Scree
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The private contractor Meridian's hunters enter the valley, and Kestrel witnesses them burn a cabin and interrogate a herder. He saves the herder, burning his own invisibility for good. The beat is the point of no return—staying hidden now means complicity.

chapters.title: Monsoon Weather
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Flying in against advice, Mara reaches the valley and confronts Kestrel with what she's learned: her father may have gone upstream to undo his own fraud. Kestrel tells her the truth about his blacklisting—a client he abandoned to die. The beat is two liars choosing honesty as the first rain falls.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Mara's POV, alternating. They climb the river gorge to its source and find the survey team's final camp: two dead, and her father Aldous alive but injured, guarding the corrected survey and a confession. Meridian's hunters close in. The beat is grief, vindication, and a race against rising water.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The monsoon hits in full. Aldous, unable to travel, gives Kestrel the documents and his testimony and stays behind with Suri's people, who shelter him. Kestrel leads Mara down the flooded gorge as Meridian's men pursue. The beat is desperate flight where the river is both enemy and ally.

chapters.title: The Gorge Decides
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Climax: cornered above a cataract, Kestrel uses his disgraced rescue skills—ropes, river-reading, the very judgment that once failed him—to get Mara and the documents across, then turns the hunters' own crossing against them. The beat is mastery redeemed: the failure that broke him becomes the thing that saves her.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, closing with Mara's. At the trailhead he phones the authorities and surrenders, handing over the corrected survey and Aldous's confession. Weeks later, the fraud unravels publicly; Kestrel faces charges but finds the valley standing witness for him. The beat is justice chosen over freedom, and a man finally visible.
